issue_context.title: API: define better type (enum) and remove `archive.Changes` from the API
issue_context.body:
For a follow-up, we must look into this signature.
https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/44964#discussion_r1146191510

When working on the CLI I was wondering why `pkg/archive` was imported in some location where I wouldn't expect it, and I stumbled upon this code; https://github.com/docker/cli/blob/14482589df194a86b2ee07df643ba3277b40df7d/cli/command/container/formatter_diff.go#L56-L67

```go
func (d *diffContext) Type() string {
	var kind string
	switch d.c.Kind {
	case archive.ChangeModify:
		kind = "C"
	case archive.ChangeAdd:
		kind = "A"
	case archive.ChangeDelete:
		kind = "D"
	}
	return kind
}
```

It turns out that the Client returns its own type for this, but that type does not have the enum values;
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/1855a55d8c3cba353e6007f0ab355004ebe478d4/client/container_diff.go#L12
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/1855a55d8c3cba353e6007f0ab355004ebe478d4/api/types/container/container_changes.go#L11

We should consider to either

- add the enums to the API types
- have the backend return the correct type
- have a utility to convert the type
- (possibly alias one for the other if needed)

_Originally posted by @thaJeztah in https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/44964#discussion_r1146191510_

review_comments: Should we do something different here to make it more obvious when it's an unknown value?

I was considering that; for now I stuck with what the CLI already used; https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/45235#issue-1647516498

And wasn't sure what else to put here (`"-"` ? `"?"` ? `<unknown>` ?) WDYT?

I personally like something really really verbose that'll definitely screw up formatting like `<unknown>` or `<invalid>` because it increases the chances that someone notices (because it's definitely an error _somewhere_ if we run into that case) :sweat_smile:

I guess the alternative _could be_ to 

- not implement the stringer interface, and instead make this a `Change()` with a `(string, error)` return.
- return `strconv.Itoa()` to return the numeric value

I do like the stringer interface though (is handy to have), and if we return an error, we also need to take into account "what if we add more options in future?" So yeah, perhaps `<unknown>` is the way to go 🤔
